app.title: Prototype 3
app.tagline: Design the sensor network of a real monument, then see what the ARGUS experts did.

steps.label: Progress
home.intro: Old buildings are in danger from water, weather, insects and people. Today you choose the sensors that watch over one of them. Then you find out what the ARGUS experts really installed.
home.how1: Read the story of the monument.
home.how2: Spend your coins on sensors that can warn us about three dangers.
home.how3: Replay a real alarm from 2026: would your sensors have noticed?
home.how4: Compare your choices with the real ARGUS sensors.
home.levelHelp: Experts rated every danger at this monument, from Low to Catastrophic. More serious dangers come with more coins, as real monitoring budgets grow with the risk.
story.mission: Protect the monument from three dangers. You have {coins} to spend on sensors.
mission.heading: Build your sensor network
mission.needOne: Add at least one sensor first.
reveal.heading: What ARGUS really installed
reveal.intro: ARGUS has {n} instruments at this monument. Some sit together on one device and measure several things at once.
reveal.satelliteNote: One of them is not on the building: it is a layer of satellite images.
reveal.tableCaption: Your sensors next to the ARGUS sensors
reveal.noWrong: There is no single right answer. The real experts had to choose too. Every difference is a good question to talk about.
reveal.promptMany: ARGUS installed {n} × {name}. Why might one not be enough?
reveal.promptOnlyYou: You chose: {name}. ARGUS did not install one here. What would it add?
reveal.promptOnlyArgus: ARGUS installed: {name}, and you did not. Which danger could it be watching?

report.homeText: If you notice a crack, a damp patch or damage, make a card to show to a guard or the site staff.
report.title: Observation report
report.intro: Seen something at a monument that worries you? Fill in this card. Show it to a guard or the site staff, or send it to the people responsible for the monument. The game itself sends nothing: if you send it, it goes from your own email.
report.note: Describe it in a few words (optional)
report.noteHelp: For example: which wall, how big, what colour. Please do not write people's names.
report.whereHelp: Tap the map to put the pin on the spot, then drag the pin to adjust it. Or choose a part of the site:
report.pin: The spot where you saw it. Drag to move it.
report.mapHint: Tap the map to mark the spot
report.photoHelp: The photo stays on this device and only goes on your card. It is not sent anywhere and is not kept after you close the game.
report.photoAlt: Your photo of what you saw
report.needWhere: Mark the spot on the map, or choose a part of the site.
report.needWhen: Choose the day you saw it. It cannot be in the future.
report.cardStaff: For the guard or the site staff: this is what a visitor noticed, not an expert's diagnosis. Please check the spot.
report.saveHelp: The data file is for site staff. It uses the format ARGUS has for condition assessments. The photo is not in it.
report.saved: The file was saved on this device.
report.mineHelp: Kept only on this device, without photos.

consequence.view3dAlso: The other places of this monument in 3D:
view3d.sub: A 3D illustration from ARGUS, OpenStreetMap and Wikimedia data.
view3d.noteNobody: Nobody watching: damp rises from the ground under Room 215, salt crystallises and pushes the small stones out, and plants root in the wall tops. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteWatched: ARGUS watching: the two soil-moisture probes under the masks mosaic show the damp within months; it is treated and the damage stays small. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.dangers: What ARGUS watches at this house
view3d.noCheck: ARGUS's risk model: no recent check
view3d.credits: Imagery © Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics · Terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Outlines © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) · Rooms, sensors and dangers: ARGUS · Mosaic photos: Olaf Tausch (public domain), Kevin Stroup (CC BY 3.0), Wikimedia Commons · Wall height assumed; the other floors and all damage are an illustration
view3d.fxDangers: Shown for ARGUS's dangers here: {list}. An illustration, not a forecast.
view3d.fxNote_rain: Rain soaks the stone and runs into the ground; the walls darken as they get wet.
view3d.fxNote_acidrain: Rain made acid by polluted air: it soaks the stone and leaves it darker and grimier.
view3d.fxNote_flood: Heavy rain, and water rising over the lowest floors.
view3d.fxNote_storm: A storm: driving rain, gusts and lightning.
view3d.fxNote_wind: Wind carrying sand and salt sweeps over the walls and wears the stone.
view3d.fxNote_heat: A heatwave: the air shimmers and the stone bakes and bleaches in the sun.
view3d.fxNote_sun: Strong sunlight, day after day: the colours slowly fade.
view3d.fxNote_frost: Snow and frost, then the thaw. Water that freezes in the cracks pushes them apart, again and again.
view3d.fxNote_quake: An earthquake: the ground shakes, dust and stones fall from the wall tops.
view3d.fxNote_slide: The slope gives way: rocks roll down and dust rises.
view3d.fxNote_walls: Ancient walls without a roof: stones loosen and fall from their tops, and dust trickles down.
view3d.fxNote_creep: The ground on the slope slowly slides downhill, a tear opens across it and the walls on it tilt: 50 years in 12 seconds, at an assumed 1 cm a year.
view3d.fxNote_sink: The ground under the buildings slowly settles: the middle sinks, the walls lean in, and floors and walls crack where it bends. 50 years in 12 seconds, at an assumed 8 mm a year.
view3d.fxNote_cellar: Down into one of the cellars dug under the hill (their shapes are ARGUS's; their surface is drawn, not photographed). Pieces of the roof come away and fall to the floor, and the ground above sinks into a hollow. Which stretch caves in, and how much, is an illustration.
view3d.fxNote_damp: Damp air and water from the ground: mist hangs low, and the damp rises in the walls and falls again.
view3d.fxNote_fire: A fire in the building: flames out of the roof, smoke rising.
view3d.fxNote_wildfire: A wildfire around the place: flames in the vegetation, smoke over everything.
view3d.fxNote_smog: Polluted air: haze, soot settling on the stone, the surfaces darkening.
view3d.fxNote_plants: Plants root in the walls and grow; cut back, they come again.
view3d.fxNote_visitors: Many visitors walking through: their feet wear the floors.
view3d.creditsArgus: Satellite imagery © Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics · 3D model of the house and terrain: ARGUS (the modern shelters over the mosaics are left out so the floors can be seen) · Beyond the model: AWS Terrain Tiles, outlines © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) · Rooms, sensors and dangers: ARGUS · All damage is an illustration
view3d.subArgus: ARGUS's own 3D model of the place. The damage is an illustration.
view3d.canvasPlace: {place} in 3D. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to look around.
view3d.noteNobody_floor: Nobody watching: thousands of feet wear a path into the old floor. Its stones grow smooth and low, then come loose. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteNobody_stone: Nobody watching: wind, salt and heat wear the stone. It fades, fills with small holes, and a dark crust grows where rain never washes it. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteNobody_lean: Nobody watching: the wall by the tiltmeter leans a little more each year, then cracks open. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteNobody_tree: Nobody watching: trees and bushes grow over the walls. Their roots open the joints, and a storm can bring a branch down on them. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteNobody_fresco: Nobody watching: damp climbs up the walls, salt leaves a white line, and the paint and plaster flake off. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteNobody_crack: Nobody watching: the crack by the sensor grows longer and wider every winter, and the stones along it come loose. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteNobody_none: Nobody watching: the weather slowly wears the stone, and plants root in the walls. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.noteWatchedAny: ARGUS watching: the sensors here show the change early; it is looked after and the damage stays small. An illustration, not a prediction.
view3d.sizeDamp: Damp {h} m up the walls. Rising damp usually stops at 0.5–1.5 m above the ground.
view3d.sizeCrack: The crack {mm} mm wider and {m} m long, if it opens 0.5 mm a year: an assumption, as ARGUS's crack readings have no confirmed unit yet. In a cared-for building, such as Florence's dome, cracks grow about 6 mm a century.
view3d.sizeLean: Leaning {deg}° more, if it leans 0.05° more each year: an assumption, as no source gives a rate. A historic wall leaning 2–3° has been judged dangerous.
view3d.sizeStone: About {mm} mm of the stone's surface gone: marble and limestone lose about 0.5–5 mm a century, more by the sea. Too little to see from here; up close, the carved detail softens.
view3d.sizeFloor: The floor polished smooth and pale about {m} m around where people come in: how far the path reaches is drawn, not measured.
view3d.sizePlants: Plants on {p}% of the wall tops.
view3d.legend: The red is a sign: it shows where the monument is being damaged. The stone does not turn red.
view3d.sensorsNote: The small squares are ARGUS's real sensors. Press one to see what it is.
view3d.sensorAlarm: This sensor raised the day's alarm.

view3d.kid_crack: ⚡ The crack opens a little more every winter.
view3d.kid_lean: ↗️ The wall leans a little more every year.
